note: Meta-Reasoning (arXiv 2609.38147v1, 'Thinking Before Thinking', stamped 29 Sep 2026). Data numbers on screen: 18% (budget share used by direct control, GPT-5.5, ProgramBench, 1200 calls), 63.7% and 71.5% (mean per-problem test-pass rate on ProgramBench with GPT-5.5 at 1200 calls, direct control and meta-reasoning) and 12 (matched comparisons at the main budgets). All are the authors' own runs. Budgets are nominal model-call budgets, not tokens, time or FLOPs; the video makes no cost or efficiency claim (App. A). The Codex figure (58.0%) is not used: Codex is an external product with budget accounting added and without the read-only git tool the authors' two agents get (sec 5.2, App. G.2, App. I); the matched comparison is direct control. Every other digit on screen is a model name (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Opus 4.8), the arXiv id, or a source tag (section, page, figure).

numbers.18: Direct Control Agent with GPT-5.5 on ProgramBench uses 'only about 18% of the 1200-call allowance' (sec 6.2, p. 10). A share of the nominal call budget, one model on one benchmark; the line says 'with one model' and 'about'.
numbers.63.7: Direct Control Agent, GPT-5.5, ProgramBench, 1200-call budget: 63.7% mean per-problem test-pass rate, the share of hidden test cases on which the rebuilt program matches the reference, averaged over problems (Table 1, p. 11; sec 1, p. 2; metric defined in sec 5.1, p. 8).
numbers.71.5: Meta-Reasoning Agent, same setting and metric: 71.5% (Table 1, p. 11; sec 1, p. 2; sec 6.2, p. 10). The video names the setting (ProgramBench, GPT-5.5) and uses no superlative: it is not the largest gain in Table 1 (Gemini 3.1 Pro gains 8.6 on IMO ProofBench-Advanced and 9.2 on LongCoT-mini, which sec 6.1 calls the largest single gain over direct control).
numbers.12: Matched comparisons (4 benchmarks x 3 models) at the main budgets (100 calls on the reasoning benchmarks, 1200 on ProgramBench), all with higher point estimates for meta-reasoning (sec 1, p. 2; sec 6.1 Finding, p. 10; Table 1, p. 11). Not tested for significance per comparison (App. A, p. 20).

claims.l01: Sec 3.5 (p. 6) and sec 7.1 (p. 14): the Meta-Reasoning Agent and the Direct Control Agent 'call the same models, dispatch the same workers, and draw on the same allowance, differing only in how the run is directed'; 'every matched setting improves'. 'Same budget' is the same nominal model-call budget (sec 3.5); l08 says 'call budget', and l09 shows direct control spends far less of it. 'At the main budgets, every score rose': all 12 matched comparisons at 100 calls (reasoning) and 1200 calls (ProgramBench) have higher point estimates (sec 1, p. 2; sec 6.1 Finding, p. 10). At smaller budgets it does not hold (sec 6.2, p. 11: Opus 4.8 trails at 400 calls, GPT-5.5 slightly behind at the smallest ProgramBench budget); l14 says the overhead can hurt at small budgets. The 'main budgets' tag sits over the 12 tiles, whose rise lengths come from Table 1.
claims.l02: Abstract (p. 1): 'Each step in the run brings new control choices, like which partial work to build on, whether to start fresh, or when to stop.' 'Keep, restart, or stop' is the plain form of that list.
claims.l03: Sec 8 (p. 16), receipt crop: 'As runs grow longer, that decision becomes work in its own right.' The crop holds only that PDF line ('well it does the work. As runs grow longer, that decision becomes work in its own right.'); no digits.
claims.l04: Sec 1 (p. 2): existing agents often interleave these decisions with the object-level work, 'taking each control decision in a single step conditioned on their accumulating history'. Sec 3.5 (p. 6): the Direct Control Agent 'chooses each action in single turn over the accumulated history'.
claims.l05: Sec 1 (p. 2): 'Our Meta-Reasoning Agent separates the workers, which do the task-level work, from the controller, which decides what work to assign.' Figure 1 (p. 1). The signal box, locomotives and switches are a picture only.
claims.l06: Sec 3.3 (p. 5): 'Each control cycle has four sequential stages: Assess, Propose, Evaluate, and Dispatch.' The levers name the stages only; no stage is shown as more important.
claims.l07: Sec 1 (p. 2): 'The controller keeps a compact assessment of progress. Full worker outputs remain in persistent memory.' Sec 3.1 (p. 4): every artifact is stored with a stable identifier; sec 3.3 (p. 5): 'Between cycles, only a compact state is persisted.' Dispatch gives each worker the artifacts it needs (sec 3.3); the departing train with two wagons pictures that. No character counts on screen, and no claim that the history length caused the plateau (sec 6.5, p. 13: 'we did not test it directly').
claims.l08: Sec 3.5 (p. 6) and sec 5.2 (pp. 8 to 9): the Direct Control Agent uses the same workers and the same interfaces for delegation, context selection, artifact writing and stopping; both systems receive the same nominal model-call budget ('call budget'); same underlying models (sec 5.3). Equal call budgets are not equal token cost, latency or FLOPs (sec 3.5; App. A). The comparison changes staging, state compression and memory access together (sec 3.5; App. A).
claims.l09: Sec 6.2 (p. 10): with GPT-5.5 on ProgramBench, direct control 'uses only about 18% of the 1200-call allowance. Across models, meta-reasoning uses roughly 89% to 101% at this setting.' 'Almost all' covers that range; the right tank drains to an estimate of 0.9 and never past empty.
claims.l10: Sec 6.2 (p. 11), receipt crop: with Opus 4.8 on ProgramBench, 'direct control roughly doubles its calls used over the sweep, from 376 to 768. Its score rises only modestly, from 62.7% to 65.3%, and peaks at the intermediate budget. Continuing to work is not enough; what the agent does next also matters.' The budget grows from 400 to 1200 calls (sec 5.3). The bar and the budget marker share one absolute calls axis without tick labels. The crop is the single PDF line 'at the intermediate budget. Continuing to work is not enough; what the agent does next also matters.'; the next line ('Meta-reasoning does not win at every budget ...') is outside it.
claims.l11: Table 1 (p. 11) and sec 1 (p. 2): ProgramBench with GPT-5.5 at 1200 calls, mean per-problem test-pass rate 63.7% (Direct Control Agent) and 71.5% (Meta-Reasoning Agent). ProgramBench scores the fraction of hidden test cases on which the rebuilt program matches the reference (sec 5.1, p. 8); 'on average' and the 'mean test-pass rate' tag say it is an average over problems, not solved programs. Bars start at zero. The line names the setting and makes no 'best' claim: it is the largest ProgramBench gain of the three models, not the largest in Table 1.
claims.l12: Sec 6.2 (p. 10): 'As the ProgramBench allowance grows from 400 to 1200 calls, meta-reasoning with GPT-5.5 rises from 64.1% to 71.5%. Direct control stays near 64% across the sweep.' Drawn as a sketch after Figure 3 with no tick labels or middle point.
claims.l13: Sec 1 (p. 2): 'meta-reasoning yields higher point estimates in all 12 matched comparisons' at the main allowances (100 calls reasoning, 1200 ProgramBench). Table 1 (p. 11) gives per-cell gains from 0.4 to 9.2 points. App. A (p. 20): positive point estimates 'do not establish significance for every difference'. 'Some gains are small' covers this.
claims.l14: Abstract (p. 1), receipt crop: 'It keeps improving over the tested budget ranges where direct control plateaus, though its overhead can hurt at small budgets.' Sec 6.2 (p. 11): with Opus 4.8 it trails direct control at 400 calls; GPT-5.5 is slightly behind at the smallest ProgramBench budget. App. A (p. 20): 'The experiments cover three frontier models and four benchmarks' and give no generalization to weaker models. The crossing at the small-budget end of the sketch is GPT-5.5 on ProgramBench, drawn without figures.
claims.l15: Sec 8 (p. 16): 'An agent's performance therefore depends on how well it decides what work is worth doing, alongside how well it does the work.' The line is the plain form of that sentence.
